## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(stringr)

#' Compute Halstead Complexity Measures for MS SQL Queries
#'
#' This function takes an MS SQL query as a string and computes various 
#' Halstead complexity measures including vocabulary, length, volume, 
#' difficulty, and effort.
#'
#' @param sql_query A character string containing the SQL query
#' @return A data frame with one row containing Halstead complexity measures
#' @examples
#' query <- "SELECT name, age FROM users WHERE age > 25 ORDER BY name"
#' halstead_complexity_sql(query)
halstead_complexity_sql <- function(sql_query) {
  
  # Define SQL operators (keywords, symbols, functions)
  sql_operators <- c(
    # SQL Keywords
    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "ORDER", "BY", "GROUP", "HAVING", 
    "INSERT", "INTO", "VALUES", "UPDATE", "SET", "DELETE", "CREATE",
    "TABLE", "DROP", "ALTER", "INDEX", "VIEW", "PROCEDURE", "FUNCTION",
    "TRIGGER", "DATABASE", "SCHEMA", "CONSTRAINT", "PRIMARY", "KEY",
    "FOREIGN", "REFERENCES", "UNIQUE", "NOT", "NULL", "DEFAULT",
    "CHECK", "AUTO_INCREMENT", "IDENTITY", "CLUSTERED", "NONCLUSTERED",
    
    # Joins
    "JOIN", "INNER", "LEFT", "RIGHT", "FULL", "OUTER", "CROSS", "ON",
    
    # Logical operators
    "AND", "OR", "IN", "EXISTS", "BETWEEN", "LIKE", "IS",
    
    # Comparison operators
    "=", "!=", "<>", "<", ">", "<=", ">=",
    
    # Arithmetic operators
    "+", "-", "*", "/", "%",
    
    # Aggregate functions
    "COUNT", "SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX", "STDEV", "VAR",
    
    # String functions
    "LEN", "LENGTH", "SUBSTRING", "SUBSTR", "UPPER", "LOWER", "TRIM",
    "LTRIM", "RTRIM", "REPLACE", "CHARINDEX", "PATINDEX", "CONCAT",
    
    # Date functions
    "GETDATE", "DATEADD", "DATEDIFF", "YEAR", "MONTH", "DAY",
    "DATEPART", "CAST", "CONVERT",
    
    # Conditional
    "CASE", "WHEN", "THEN", "ELSE", "END", "IF",
    
    # Other functions
    "ISNULL", "COALESCE", "NULLIF", "IIF",
    
    # Punctuation and symbols
    "(", ")", ",", ";", ".", "[", "]", "'", "\"",
    
    # Set operations
    "UNION", "INTERSECT", "EXCEPT", "ALL", "DISTINCT",
    
    # Subquery keywords
    "ANY", "SOME", "AS", "ALIAS",
    
    # Window functions
    "OVER", "PARTITION", "ROW_NUMBER", "RANK", "DENSE_RANK",
    
    # Data types (common ones)
    "INT", "INTEGER", "VARCHAR", "CHAR", "TEXT", "DATETIME", "DATE",
    "TIME", "DECIMAL", "NUMERIC", "FLOAT", "REAL", "BIT", "MONEY"
  )
  
  # Preprocess the query
  # Remove comments
  sql_query <- gsub("--.*$", "", sql_query, perl = TRUE)
  sql_query <- gsub("/\\*.*?\\*/", "", sql_query, perl = TRUE)
  
  # Convert to uppercase for consistent matching
  sql_upper <- toupper(sql_query)
  
  # Split into tokens - this is a simplified tokenizer
  # It splits on whitespace and common punctuation, keeping the punctuation
  tokens <- unlist(str_split(sql_upper, "\\s+"))
  tokens <- tokens[tokens != ""]  # Remove empty strings
  
  # Further split tokens that contain punctuation
  all_tokens <- c()
  for (token in tokens) {
    # Split on punctuation but keep the punctuation
    parts <- str_split(token, "([(),.;\\[\\]'\"=<>!+\\-*/%])", perl = TRUE)[[1]]
    parts <- parts[parts != ""]
    all_tokens <- c(all_tokens, parts)
  }
  
  # Remove empty tokens
  all_tokens <- all_tokens[all_tokens != ""]
  
  # Convert operators to uppercase for matching
  sql_operators_upper <- toupper(sql_operators)
  
  # Identify operators and operands
  operators <- c()
  operands <- c()
  
  for (token in all_tokens) {
    if (token %in% sql_operators_upper) {
      operators <- c(operators, token)
    } else if (!str_detect(token, "^\\s*$")) {  # Not just whitespace
      # Consider it an operand (table names, column names, literals, etc.)
      operands <- c(operands, token)
    }
  }
  
  # Calculate Halstead measures
  # n1 = number of distinct operators
  n1 <- length(unique(operators))
  
  # n2 = number of distinct operands  
  n2 <- length(unique(operands))
  
  # N1 = total number of operators
  N1 <- length(operators)
  
  # N2 = total number of operands
  N2 <- length(operands)
  
  # Program vocabulary
  n <- n1 + n2
  
  # Program length
  N <- N1 + N2
  
  # Calculated estimated program length
  Nhat <- n1 * log2(n1) + n2 * log2(n2)
  
  # Volume
  Volume <- N * log2(n)
  
  # Difficulty
  Difficulty <- (n1 / 2) * (N2 / n2)
  
  # Effort
  Effort <- Difficulty * Volume
  
  # Handle edge cases
  if (is.infinite(Nhat) || is.nan(Nhat)) Nhat <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Volume) || is.nan(Volume)) Volume <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Difficulty) || is.nan(Difficulty)) Difficulty <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Effort) || is.nan(Effort)) Effort <- 0
  
  # Create result data frame
  result <- data.frame(
    n_1 = n1,
    n_2 = n2,
    N_1 = N1,
    N_2 = N2,
    n = n,
    N = N,
    Nhat = round(Nhat, 2),
    Volume = round(Volume, 2),
    Difficulty = round(Difficulty, 2),
    Effort = round(Effort, 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(result)
}

# Example usage:
# Simple query
query1 <- "SELECT name, age FROM users WHERE age > 25"
result1 <- halstead_complexity_sql(query1)
print("Simple query results:")
print(result1)

# More complex query
query2 <- "
SELECT u.name, u.age, COUNT(o.id) as order_count, AVG(o.total) as avg_order
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.age BETWEEN 18 AND 65
  AND u.status = 'active'
GROUP BY u.name, u.age
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 5
ORDER BY avg_order DESC
"
result2 <- halstead_complexity_sql(query2)
print("\nComplex query results:")
print(result2)
```

library(stringr)

#' Compute Halstead Complexity Measures for MS SQL Queries
#'
#' This function takes an MS SQL query as a string and computes various 
#' Halstead complexity measures including vocabulary, length, volume, 
#' difficulty, and effort.
#'
#' @param sql_query A character string containing the SQL query
#' @return A data frame with one row containing Halstead complexity measures
#' @examples
#' query <- "SELECT name, age FROM users WHERE age > 25 ORDER BY name"
#' halstead_complexity_sql(query)
halstead_complexity_sql <- function(sql_query) {
  
  # Define SQL operators (keywords, symbols, functions)
  sql_operators <- c(
    # SQL Keywords
    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "ORDER", "BY", "GROUP", "HAVING", 
    "INSERT", "INTO", "VALUES", "UPDATE", "SET", "DELETE", "CREATE",
    "TABLE", "DROP", "ALTER", "INDEX", "VIEW", "PROCEDURE", "FUNCTION",
    "TRIGGER", "DATABASE", "SCHEMA", "CONSTRAINT", "PRIMARY", "KEY",
    "FOREIGN", "REFERENCES", "UNIQUE", "NOT", "NULL", "DEFAULT",
    "CHECK", "AUTO_INCREMENT", "IDENTITY", "CLUSTERED", "NONCLUSTERED",
    
    # Joins
    "JOIN", "INNER", "LEFT", "RIGHT", "FULL", "OUTER", "CROSS", "ON",
    
    # Logical operators
    "AND", "OR", "IN", "EXISTS", "BETWEEN", "LIKE", "IS",
    
    # Comparison operators
    "=", "!=", "<>", "<", ">", "<=", ">=",
    
    # Arithmetic operators
    "+", "-", "*", "/", "%",
    
    # Aggregate functions
    "COUNT", "SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX", "STDEV", "VAR",
    
    # String functions
    "LEN", "LENGTH", "SUBSTRING", "SUBSTR", "UPPER", "LOWER", "TRIM",
    "LTRIM", "RTRIM", "REPLACE", "CHARINDEX", "PATINDEX", "CONCAT",
    
    # Date functions
    "GETDATE", "DATEADD", "DATEDIFF", "YEAR", "MONTH", "DAY",
    "DATEPART", "CAST", "CONVERT",
    
    # Conditional
    "CASE", "WHEN", "THEN", "ELSE", "END", "IF",
    
    # Other functions
    "ISNULL", "COALESCE", "NULLIF", "IIF",
    
    # Punctuation and symbols
    "(", ")", ",", ";", ".", "[", "]", "'", "\"",
    
    # Set operations
    "UNION", "INTERSECT", "EXCEPT", "ALL", "DISTINCT",
    
    # Subquery keywords
    "ANY", "SOME", "AS", "ALIAS",
    
    # Window functions
    "OVER", "PARTITION", "ROW_NUMBER", "RANK", "DENSE_RANK",
    
    # Data types (common ones)
    "INT", "INTEGER", "VARCHAR", "CHAR", "TEXT", "DATETIME", "DATE",
    "TIME", "DECIMAL", "NUMERIC", "FLOAT", "REAL", "BIT", "MONEY"
  )
  
  # Preprocess the query
  # Remove comments
  sql_query <- gsub("--.*$", "", sql_query)
  sql_query <- gsub("/\\*.*?\\*/", "", sql_query)
  
  # Convert to uppercase for consistent matching
  sql_upper <- toupper(sql_query)
  
  # Tokenize the SQL query
  # Use a more sophisticated approach to split while preserving operators
  # Replace punctuation with spaces around them, then split
  sql_tokenized <- sql_upper
  
  # Add spaces around operators to ensure they're separated
  operators_to_separate <- c("\\(", "\\)", ",", ";", "\\.", "\\[", "\\]", 
                            "'", "\"", "=", "!=", "<>", "<=", ">=", "<", ">", 
                            "\\+", "-", "\\*", "/", "%")
  
  for (op in operators_to_separate) {
    sql_tokenized <- gsub(paste0("(", op, ")"), " \\1 ", sql_tokenized)
  }
  
  # Split on whitespace and remove empty tokens
  all_tokens <- unlist(str_split(sql_tokenized, "\\s+"))
  all_tokens <- all_tokens[all_tokens != "" & !str_detect(all_tokens, "^\\s*$")]
  
  # Convert operators to uppercase for matching
  sql_operators_upper <- toupper(sql_operators)
  
  # Identify operators and operands
  operators <- c()
  operands <- c()
  
  for (token in all_tokens) {
    if (token %in% sql_operators_upper) {
      operators <- c(operators, token)
    } else if (!str_detect(token, "^\\s*$")) {  # Not just whitespace
      # Consider it an operand (table names, column names, literals, etc.)
      operands <- c(operands, token)
    }
  }
  
  # Calculate Halstead measures
  # n1 = number of distinct operators
  n1 <- length(unique(operators))
  
  # n2 = number of distinct operands  
  n2 <- length(unique(operands))
  
  # N1 = total number of operators
  N1 <- length(operators)
  
  # N2 = total number of operands
  N2 <- length(operands)
  
  # Program vocabulary
  n <- n1 + n2
  
  # Program length
  N <- N1 + N2
  
  # Calculated estimated program length
  Nhat <- n1 * log2(n1) + n2 * log2(n2)
  
  # Volume
  Volume <- N * log2(n)
  
  # Difficulty
  Difficulty <- (n1 / 2) * (N2 / n2)
  
  # Effort
  Effort <- Difficulty * Volume
  
  # Handle edge cases
  if (is.infinite(Nhat) || is.nan(Nhat)) Nhat <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Volume) || is.nan(Volume)) Volume <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Difficulty) || is.nan(Difficulty)) Difficulty <- 0
  if (is.infinite(Effort) || is.nan(Effort)) Effort <- 0
  
  # Create result data frame
  result <- data.frame(
    n_1 = n1,
    n_2 = n2,
    N_1 = N1,
    N_2 = N2,
    n = n,
    N = N,
    Nhat = round(Nhat, 2),
    Volume = round(Volume, 2),
    Difficulty = round(Difficulty, 2),
    Effort = round(Effort, 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(result)
}

# Let's also create a debug version to see the tokens
halstead_complexity_sql_debug <- function(sql_query) {
  # Same preprocessing as main function
  sql_query <- gsub("--.*$", "", sql_query)
  sql_query <- gsub("/\\*.*?\\*/", "", sql_query)
  sql_upper <- toupper(sql_query)
  
  # Same tokenization
  sql_tokenized <- sql_upper
  operators_to_separate <- c("\\(", "\\)", ",", ";", "\\.", "\\[", "\\]", 
                            "'", "\"", "=", "!=", "<>", "<=", ">=", "<", ">", 
                            "\\+", "-", "\\*", "/", "%")
  
  for (op in operators_to_separate) {
    sql_tokenized <- gsub(paste0("(", op, ")"), " \\1 ", sql_tokenized)
  }
  
  all_tokens <- unlist(str_split(sql_tokenized, "\\s+"))
  all_tokens <- all_tokens[all_tokens != "" & !str_detect(all_tokens, "^\\s*$")]
  
  sql_operators_upper <- toupper(c(
    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "ORDER", "BY", "GROUP", "HAVING", 
    "INSERT", "INTO", "VALUES", "UPDATE", "SET", "DELETE", "CREATE",
    "=", "!=", "<>", "<", ">", "<=", ">=", "+", "-", "*", "/", "%",
    "(", ")", ",", ";", ".", "[", "]", "'", "\"", "AND", "OR", "NOT"
  ))
  
  operators <- c()
  operands <- c()
  
  for (token in all_tokens) {
    if (token %in% sql_operators_upper) {
      operators <- c(operators, token)
    } else {
      operands <- c(operands, token)
    }
  }
  
  cat("All tokens:", paste(all_tokens, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("Operators:", paste(operators, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("Operands:", paste(operands, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  return(list(tokens = all_tokens, operators = operators, operands = operands))
}
